clue.text: Having good times round City, planned meeting to impregnate

indicators.note: the phrase for good times is placed around the City's letters, which sit within it

parts.note: having good times is having fun
EC is the postcode for the City of London
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: A romantic outing in town, timed to lead to conception.
explanation.walkthrough: The EC postcode covers the City of London, the capital's financial district, so 'City' gives those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To fertilise or make fruitful is the sense of both words, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Trimming hair down there?

parts.note: fur is an animal's hair
below means down there, underneath

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about intimate grooming.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bikini wax; a furbelow is actually a frill or flounce on a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a ruffled strip of decoration on clothing, a kind of trimming.

clue.text: Animal, leopard perhaps, consuming duck on island

indicators.note: the big cat eats, so takes inside itself, the duck's letter

parts.note: a leopard is an example of a cat
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A leopard on an island eating a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts O inside CAT to give COAT, then I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a long-snouted South American mammal related to the raccoon.

clue.text: Holy man in a camp moves about, having many relationships

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A holy man wanders through a camp, forming many bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an excessive sexual appetite would have many lovers, so the phrase describes the adjective.

clue.text: This spake Zarathustra in article about goddess

indicators.note: the article's two letters go about, on either side of, the goddess

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Vesta is the Roman goddess of the hearth

explanation.surface: A nod to Nietzsche's Thus Spake Zarathustra, as if an article discussed a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Zarathustra (Zoroaster) is the Persian prophet whose scriptures, the Avesta, are written in this ancient Iranian language.
explanation.definitionFit: Avestan is the old Iranian tongue of the Zoroastrian scriptures, the language the prophet would have used.

clue.text: Saw stuff taken to European gourmand

indicators.note: the word for stuffing is attached after the other pieces

parts.note: a greedy eater is a pig
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A tool being stuffed into a greedy European diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb or a tool, but here it is a noun meaning a saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, and an epigram is a pithy, witty remark.

clue.text: Go mad in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for mad

explanation.surface: Someone losing their mind after leaving work.
explanation.walkthrough: BATS read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go at something is to have an attempt, as in 'have a stab at it'.

clue.text: Nice heads hosting adult conversation?

indicators.note: the heads take in, as a host would, the adult's letter

parts.note: in Nice, in France, tête is the word for head, so two heads are TETE TETE
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Pleasant heads giving room to a grown-up chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, so its heads are French. The question mark flags the phrase's literal 'head to head' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private talk between two people, literally head to head.

clue.text: Suspicion bug's first about at hospital

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word bug is used

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a hospital has a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A breath can mean a slight hint, as in a breath of scandal, which is a suspicion.

clue.text: Vamp explored in bed without love: she not really being fair?

indicators.note: to vamp is to patch up or improvise, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A seductress who romped in bed without real love, and is she even fair?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vamp' looks like the seductress, but it is the anagram signal; 'without' means outside, the O joining the letters of EXPLORED IN BED.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose fair hair comes from bleach is not naturally fair-haired.

clue.text: Silver coin and money supply in kingdom

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish silver coin
M, as in M1 or M3, denotes measures of the money supply

explanation.surface: A kingdom's coinage and supply of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or domain ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Focal point in long poem with short introduction

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: an entrée is an introduction, a way in

explanation.surface: Literary criticism about a long poem with a brief preface.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point above an earthquake's origin, so generally the central point.

clue.text: Mining Derbyshire pit he thought to provide descriptive phrase

indicators.note: mining means digging into the words to extract letters hidden within them

explanation.surface: A Derbyshire coal pit that a man thought would supply something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mining' fits the colliery picture but signals the letters are dug out of 'DerbyshirE PIT HE Thought'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive word or label attached to a name, like 'the Great'.

clue.text: Brazilian diplomacy to be applied where there's trouble?

definitions.text: to be applied where there's trouble?

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city, so 'Brazilian' gives Rio
tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Brazilian diplomacy being deployed in a trouble spot.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'read the riot act' is to give a stern warning; the Riot Act was a British law read out to disperse crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was historically read aloud to crowds in disorder, so it is used where unrest breaks out.

clue.text: Impotent Rome a dilapidated superpower now gone

indicators.note: a dilapidated building has fallen apart, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Rome, once mighty, now feeble and crumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish dynasty's dominion was a great power for centuries until its fall after the First World War.

clue.text: Guide to fingering a brutal criminal in note

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the note's two letters

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bent, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A note pointing the finger at a brutal criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges the letters of 'brutal'. 'Fingering' suggests accusing someone, not playing an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablature is musical notation showing guitarists where to place their fingers rather than which notes to play.

clue.text: Second ballistic missile thundering

parts.note: Trident is a submarine-launched ballistic missile

explanation.surface: A second missile thundering through the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident means loud and harsh, as is a booming, thundering voice.

clue.text: Display of balance — something pronounced on slope?

indicators.note: in an across answer the thing pronounced sits on, after, the slope

parts.note: a bank is a slope
a statement is something declared or pronounced

explanation.surface: A tightrope walker's balance on display while a declaration is made on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balance' suggests poise, but it is the money in an account.
explanation.definitionFit: The paper record a lender sends shows the account's balance.

clue.text: Ecstasy smuggled in small deception

indicators.note: the drug's letter is smuggled into the word for small

parts.note: slight means small
E is the street abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A small amount of a drug smuggled through by trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight, as in sleight of hand, is trickery or cunning.

clue.text: Gunners returned to fix light

indicators.note: returned means the two letters for the gunners come back, read backwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
to clamp is to fix in place

explanation.surface: Soldiers come back to repair a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp is an intense electric lamp producing light from a spark between electrodes.

clue.text: Old player's son very good at cricket practice

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means very good
cricketers practise in the nets, enclosed batting areas

explanation.surface: A former cricketer's boy shining at net practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a sportsman, but it is a musical instrument; 'Old player's' reads as 'Old player is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinet is a small harpsichord popular in the 18th century, an old instrument.

clue.text: Helping around inside brings calm

indicators.note: the abbreviation for around goes inside the word for helping

parts.note: a plate is a helping of food, a plateful
ca, short for circa, means around

explanation.surface: Giving help to those around brings calm.
explanation.definitionFit: To calm someone is to pacify or appease them, soothing their anger.

clue.text: Charlie lives alone in retreat for notables

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the words are read in reverse

parts.note: lives means is, exists
solo means alone

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie lives as a hermit, hiding from the famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns IS SOLO back to front, giving OLOSSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossi, giant statues, can also figuratively mean towering people of great importance.

clue.text: Sporty sort to deprive captain of tuppence?

indicators.note: to deprive the captain means he loses something, letters taken from his word
of names what the captain is deprived of, the two pennies

parts.note: a skipper is a captain
tuppence is two pence, two p's

explanation.surface: Robbing a ship's captain of a couple of pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuppence is British slang for two pennies, here two letter Ps.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is someone who takes part in a winter sport on snow.

clue.text: Arbitrary rule again becomes real pain

indicators.note: arbitrary means random, so the letters are put in a random order

explanation.surface: An arbitrary rule imposed again is a real pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuralgia is sharp nerve pain, a genuine ache rather than an annoyance.

clue.text: Innocent one in place for congregation

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the church area's word

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church where the congregation sits
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A guiltless worshipper in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means unworldly and lacking experience, so innocent.

clue.text: Maybe moor by river bank

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up, an example of tying

explanation.surface: Perhaps mooring a boat beside a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moor' suggests open heathland, but it is the verb for securing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a row or level, as is a bank of seats.

clue.text: Doctor to respect line on MI6 file?

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A medic urged to show respect toward a spy agency's records.
explanation.definitionFit: A classification stamped on intelligence documents, MI6 being Britain's foreign intelligence service, marks them as highly classified.
